speakers.name: Zach Fadem (on for Andrew Charles; labelled Zach Ogden in transcript)

exchanges.question: When LTOs are brought back from the pantry (e.g. Chicken al Pastor), is the lift still as good or better than the prior run given mixed card data? And is value perception changing given generous portions and having underpriced the industry for so long?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle Honey Chicken performed better the second time around, as do many LTOs, though there is likely a point of diminishing returns around the fifth or sixth run; menu innovation has been ramped to 4x what it was a couple of years ago, with new items coming in the months ahead alongside returning favorites. The brand tracker showed solid progress on value perception across all income groups and age cohorts, and Q2 affordability scores were the best in probably the past couple of years. Value is about convenience, execution and menu innovation, not just discounting; the high-protein menu at an approachable price point is contributing and Chipotle believes it should own the protein category.

exchanges.question: Investors push back that Chipotle is doing and spending a lot to get only 1%-2% same-store sales growth; with tough comparisons and a recent slowdown, what gives management confidence that momentum picks up into 2027?
exchanges.answer: Q2 transaction growth reflected the early days of the Recipe for Growth strategy, particularly menu innovation, while investments in HEAP, throughput and hospitality are producing early proof points in guest satisfaction, food quality and operational consistency. Additional drivers (menu innovation, deeper rewards engagement, stronger brand communication, expanded group occasions) are showing green shoots and will build and layer through the second half of 2026 and into 2027. Early thinking from Arlie Sisson on digital commerce and Fernando Machado on culturally relevant branding was described as really innovative and industry changing but not shared on the call.

exchanges.question: Can you give more color on the positive low single-digit 2026 comp guide, including Q3 and the recent softening, where the trend was before the industry challenges, and the cadence from here?
exchanges.answer: Traffic improved throughout Q2 and momentum continued into the first half of July; in the second half of July comps softened by about 200 basis points around the industry Cyclospora issue. Q3 comps are expected at around plus 1%, assuming the roughly 200 basis point impact continues since its duration is hard to predict, against the toughest lap of the year; year-to-date performance plus the Q3 set-up and Q4 plans drove the raise to low single digits for the full year. Scott added that Chipotle is affected on sales but not involved in the Cyclospora issue: the implicated products are not on its menu and its lettuces are sourced in California.

exchanges.question: Has Chipotle sized the incremental capex for the store refresh program (three investment levels across roughly 1,000-1,500 North American stores) and is there any early read on sales uplift and timeline? Would Chipotle use partners rather than owning restaurants in other international markets?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle has never done an aesthetic remodel in its history; this year it is stage-gating a remodel/refresh test at several locations across several geographies at $100,000-$300,000 per restaurant to gauge consumer perception and return, with nothing to report yet and management optimistic but patient. Internationally, partnerships are being built slowly and strategically: Alshaya in the Middle East, Alsea in Latin America and SPC in Southeast Asia, through partner-operated and/or JV structures. Chipotle will continue to own and operate Western Europe and grow from that base, with the rest of the world partner-operated.

exchanges.question: Digital sales grew about 18% year over year including unit growth; was there a catalyst that unlocked this roughly four quarters ago, and is it linked to the loyalty and payment changes at the register?
exchanges.answer: It is all linked: last year's Summer of Extras showed where Chipotle has the right to win in digital and what does not work for the brand, which informed the rewards relaunch a couple of months ago that removed friction and added flexibility in earning and redeeming; this year's Summer of Extras has accelerated digital revenue, helped by being right place, right time on an emerging trend. Arlie is taking a holistic approach to digital, it is early days, and the digital commerce innovation she brings over the coming weeks and months is expected to be game changing.

exchanges.question: Should all of the HEAP labor efficiency be expected to be reinvested into the production line, and could it help drive positive traffic and front-line customer satisfaction?
exchanges.answer: Yes: HEAP yields about two to four hours of labor efficiency depending on volume, which is left in the restaurant to complete morning prep and deploy crew on the line during peak; this is translating into transaction gains in Max 15 and total sales plus better taste-of-food scores. Rollout is as aggressive as possible, reaching 2,000 restaurants by year-end with the entire portfolio hopefully completed sometime in 2027, and all new restaurants come standard with HEAP.

exchanges.question: Why is 350 company-operated openings per year the right level versus the prior ceiling of 400, and what is the gating factor to accelerating above 350?
exchanges.answer: Given U.S. white space and the ability to develop ready-now leaders, one restaurant per day is meaningful growth the organization can support without losing its opening edge; beyond 350 there could be diminishing returns in opening quality or a risk of fracturing the base. Incremental growth comes from global expansion, both company-owned Western Europe and partner-operated markets that will ramp quickly: Alshaya is already at 15 restaurants across three or four countries after a couple of years with meaningful acceleration planned for 2027, so Chipotle can still target the total growth number discussed historically.

exchanges.question: With a new Chief Brand Officer, how should the brand be positioned given the long-running For Real campaign feels stale, and will value and in-restaurant food preparation versus limited-service competitors be highlighted more prominently?
exchanges.answer: For Real was extraordinary and served the brand for many years; Fernando's work is not a 180 pivot but the next evolution, showing more of how food is prepared fresh in-restaurant, more on ingredient usage and more on cultivating a better world, with creative ambition that breaks through the sea of sameness on television. Value will be highlighted, but as the extraordinary value of the best ingredients prepared fresh daily at abundance and speed for an approachable price point, rather than price points or discounts.

exchanges.question: Does the roughly 1% Q3 comp guide with a 200 basis point Cyclospora impact imply an underlying trend of about plus 3% with the headwind assumed to persist for the rest of the quarter? And where is system Max 15 throughput for restaurants without HEAP?
exchanges.answer: Correct: the 1% guide assumes the impact continues through the rest of the quarter and the expense-line guidance was built on it; duration is very difficult to predict. HEAP restaurants do about two or three more entrees in Max 15; system-wide in-store Max 15 is in the low 20s, digital (almost 40% of sales) adds somewhere in the mid-teens, so combined Max 15 is in the low to mid-30s per restaurant per day.

exchanges.question: Can you elaborate on efforts to promote the loyalty program in-restaurant, what is working and what could improve? And do the roughly 80% of in-store transactions without loyalty correlate with lower-income guests?
exchanges.answer: No, the non-loyalty in-store transactions are broad-based rather than lower-income skewed, and converting them could deliver a meaningful lift. The current experience (opening the app, then paying by card) is clunky, so in August Curt and team will launch a one-stop pay where paying earns rewards points and guests can ask to be enrolled, executed behind the scenes without relying on restaurant teams or hurting throughput; more consumer education on the program in-restaurant is still needed.

exchanges.question: Can you elaborate on the new menu items coming in the months ahead: are they center-of-the-plate items or sides?
exchanges.answer: The culinary team has been expanded to drive thoughtful innovation that is new news rather than just pantry items; the focus is center-of-the-plate items, with teams also working on beverage, sides and desserts. Some really big ideas, glimpsed on social media in recent months, are moving through the stage-gate process and could appear on the calendar in the back half of 2026 but certainly in 2027.

exchanges.question: What were the Q2 trends by age and income cohort, are younger and lower-to-middle income guests improving relative to higher-income guests or showing frequency differences, and is there anything to call out in Q3 to date?
exchanges.answer: The younger and lower-income cohorts that were under the most pressure have improved the most; the Q1-to-Q2 improvement was broad-based but outsized in those two groups, driven by menu innovation (Chipotle Honey Chicken, Cilantro Lime Sauce), in-restaurant promotions such as the Matchday BOGO celebrating World Cup fans, and the rewards program. Scott added that Chipotle saw its highest year-over-year wallet share gains last quarter since 2024 and has taken share in each month of 2026 across all income cohorts and age groups.

exchanges.question: How is management thinking about the margin outlook beyond Q3, specifically the gap between pricing and inflation that was expected to narrow near year-end?
exchanges.answer: The price-inflation gap was widest in the first half, when pricing was around 1% and inflation in the low to mid 3% range, and it is easing in the second half under the rolling pricing strategy. In Q3 inflation should be closer to about 3% with pricing in the mid 2% range, so the gap is largely closed; from Q4 forward pricing and inflation are expected to match, removing the dislocation going forward.

exchanges.question: Were there regional or market divergences indicating a World Cup benefit in recent months? And what was learned from the methodical pricing rollout that gave comfort to trend toward the high end of the initial 1%-2% guide?
exchanges.answer: About 300 restaurants within roughly 10 miles of World Cup stadiums saw a comp benefit of 50 to 100 basis points during the tournament, but the overall quarterly impact was less than five basis points. The rolling market-by-market pricing process is working well: it lets Chipotle measure resistance precisely, adjust if needed and respond to inflation; reads on resistance and consumer feedback supported continuing to push forward, the strategy will continue, and the first-half dislocation was purely a timing effect.

exchanges.question: What is the LTO contribution to the frequency and traffic uplift versus historical benchmarks given the stepped-up cadence? And do guests gravitating to high-protein LTOs tend to be existing customers or a new cohort?
exchanges.answer: No specific LTO lifts are disclosed, but Chipotle Honey Chicken and Chicken al Pastor increased transactions from the most frequent guests visiting more often and from new guests; LTOs typically deliver hundreds of basis points of transaction lift, most of which sustains through the promotion, and post-promotion stickiness is measured; management views this as a multi-year AUV lever rather than a short spike. Scott added that LTOs bring in first-time customers, a guest who tries an LTO sees materially higher lifetime value, and existing customers come more often; the back half brings a couple more center-of-the-plate items, sides innovation and a more meaningful push into beverage, where Chipotle sees significant opportunity.
